related_questions.question: What does T2b mean in prostate cancer?
related_questions.snippet: T2a: The tumor has invaded one-half (or less) of one side of the prostate. T2b: The tumor has spread to more than one-half of one side of the prostate, but not to both sides. T2c: The cancer has invaded both sides of the prostate.

related_questions.question: What does pT2 mean in prostate cancer?
related_questions.snippet: The prostate has been removed with surgery, and the tumor was still only in the prostate [pT2]. The cancer has not spread to nearby lymph nodes [N0] or elsewhere in the body [M0]. The Grade Group is 1, and the PSA level is less than 10.

text_blocks.snippet: cT2b prostate cancer means the tumor is palpable (can be felt during a digital rectal exam) and is confined to the prostate gland, but involves more than half of one side of the prostate, though not both sides. It is considered a Stage II prostate cancer.

list.title: Clinical Stage:
list.snippet: The "c" in cT2b stands for clinical, indicating that the tumor's stage is determined by clinical examination (like a digital rectal exam) and imaging, rather than by pathology after surgery.

list.title: T2b:
list.snippet: This specific staging means the tumor has spread to more than half of one side of the prostate, but it has not yet spread to the other side.

list.title: Stage II:
list.snippet: Stage II prostate cancer means the tumor is still contained within the prostate gland, but it is large enough to be felt during a digital rectal exam (cT2).

list.title: N0M0:
list.snippet: In cT2b, N0 means there is no evidence of cancer in the nearby lymph nodes, and M0 means there is no evidence of cancer spreading to distant sites.

list.title: PSA Level:
list.snippet: The PSA level is typically less than 20 ng/mL, according to the American Cancer Society.

list.title: Grade Group:
list.snippet: The tumor's grade, determined by Gleason score, is usually 1, indicating well-differentiated cancer cells.
